upsert.title: Palladia (toceranib) for canine oral melanoma
upsert.center: Ontario Veterinary College — University of Guelph
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — listed on current OVC canine oncology trials page
upsert.contacts: OVC Clinical Trials — ovc.clinicaltrials@uoguelph.ca; official study contact form
upsert.funding: Study covers initial staging (blood work, chest x-rays and biopsy), Palladia medication, and associated dispensing/administration fees.
upsert.notes: Treatment study for biopsy-confirmed canine oral melanoma with measurable disease. OVC states dogs with previous chemotherapy are not eligible; prior melanoma vaccination is allowed. Multiple OVC visits are required.

upsert.title: MRI-guided high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) for canine limb osteosarcoma
upsert.center: Ontario Veterinary College / Hospital for Sick Children
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — listed on current OVC canine oncology trials page
upsert.contacts: OVC Clinical Trials — ovc.clinicaltrials@uoguelph.ca; official study contact form
upsert.funding: Study covers MRI(s), HIFU treatment, associated anesthesia, study biopsies and analyses.
upsert.notes: Pilot treatment study for confirmed osteosarcoma of the distal radius with no evidence of metastasis. No previous surgery or radiation for the osteosarcoma. Prior chemotherapy and/or bisphosphonate treatment is evaluated case-by-case. Requires visits to SickKids in Toronto and OVC in Guelph.

upsert.title: Porphysome nanoparticle phototherapy for feline oral squamous cell carcinoma
upsert.center: Ontario Veterinary College — University of Guelph
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — listed on current OVC feline oncology trials page
upsert.contacts: OVC Clinical Trials — ovc.clinicaltrials@uoguelph.ca; official study contact form
upsert.funding: Confirm current study-covered and owner-paid costs with the OVC Clinical Trials team.
upsert.notes: Pilot treatment study using Porphysome liposome-based nanoparticles and phototherapy for cats with confirmed oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma. The current OVC feline oncology page lists the study as active; full protocol eligibility requires investigator prescreening.

upsert.title: Intravesical IL-12 immunotherapy for canine invasive bladder cancer
upsert.center: NC State College of Veterinary Medicine
upsert.contacts: NC State Clinical Studies Core — see official trial page
upsert.funding: Pre-staging, IL-12 immunotherapy, hospitalization, anesthesia and study monitoring are provided at no cost.
upsert.notes: Experimental intravesical IL-12 immunotherapy. Metastatic UCC is permitted. Untreated and previously treated dogs may qualify; at least one month is required since last radiation or chemotherapy. No placebo group; all enrolled dogs receive immunotherapy.

upsert.title: Radiation therapy plus XCSgel immunotherapy for canine soft tissue sarcoma
upsert.center: NC State College of Veterinary Medicine
upsert.contacts: NC State Clinical Studies Core — see official trial page
upsert.funding: NC State states enrolled dogs receive free testing, treatment and follow-up, including bloodwork, CT, surgery and radiation therapy.
upsert.notes: Blinded study of standard radiation therapy plus XCSgel immunotherapy; all enrolled dogs receive surgery and radiation, while XCSgel versus placebo is blinded. Pathologic confirmation of STS required and no prior radiation or chemotherapy.

upsert.title: PIVOT-C intratumoral FVRCP vaccine therapy for feline oral tumors
upsert.center: NC State College of Veterinary Medicine
upsert.contacts: Dr. Joanne Intile / NC State — see official trial page
upsert.funding: Confirm study-covered and owner-paid costs with the investigator.
upsert.notes: 28-day pilot treatment study with weekly intratumoral FVRCP vaccine injections on days 0, 7, 14, 21 and 28. Cats cannot receive surgery or radiation while enrolled; those treatments may be considered after study completion or early exit.

upsert.title: Comparative radiotherapy approaches before amputation for canine osteosarcoma
upsert.center: NC State College of Veterinary Medicine
upsert.contacts: NC State Clinical Studies Core — see official trial page
upsert.funding: Confirm current study-covered and owner-paid costs with NC State.
upsert.notes: Large or giant breed dogs with a distal-radius bone tumor may qualify. Each enrolled dog receives a single dose of radiotherapy followed within three weeks by standard limb amputation. No prior osteosarcoma-directed therapy; no metastasis.

upsert.title: CAR T cell immunotherapy for treatment of metastatic osteosarcoma in dogs
upsert.center: Colorado State University Flint Animal Cancer Center
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — confirmed on CSU current clinical trials page and August 4, 2026 recruitment post
upsert.contacts: CSU Flint Animal Cancer Center Clinical Trials — (970) 297-4001; online clinical-trial consult form
upsert.funding: Once enrolled, study covers clinical-trial costs including diagnostics, CAR T-cell generation and infusion, and study blood collection/processing, except recheck exam fees. Screening funds and up to $2,000 for treatment of trial-related side effects are available.
upsert.notes: Confirmed osteosarcoma after primary-tumor surgery with measurable pulmonary metastases on chest radiographs. Requires adequate bloodwork and 2–3 week chemotherapy washout. Protocol includes lymphodepleting fludarabine/cyclophosphamide, IV CAR T-cell infusion, plus oral losartan and propranolol. All study visits occur at CSU.

upsert.title: Intravenous carboplatin for pain control in canine appendicular osteosarcoma
upsert.center: Colorado State University Flint Animal Cancer Center
upsert.status: Actively recruiting — listed on CSU current clinical trials page
upsert.contacts: CSU Flint Animal Cancer Center Clinical Trials — (970) 297-4001; online clinical-trial consult form
upsert.funding: Study covers pre-enrollment CBC, chemistry, urinalysis, chest and limb radiographs and tumor aspirate/biopsy; after enrollment it covers one carboplatin treatment, study rechecks, repeat bloodwork and limb radiographs, plus initial anti-nausea/anti-diarrheal medications.
upsert.notes: Single IV carboplatin treatment followed by three weeks of activity, gait, imaging and laboratory monitoring. Requires seven days on a standard oral pain regimen before enrollment and a 30-day bisphosphonate washout.
